gaps.sentence: Don't disturb him — he ___ an important video call with the client.
gaps.hint: do not disturb means it is happening now
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous: is having.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys again — this is the third time this month!
gaps.hint: third time this month connects to now
gaps.explanation: 'This is the third time' links a recent event to now, so the present perfect is required: has lost.
Visible present evidence points to a future event: 'is going to fall'.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the doctor's on Tuesday; I made the appointment yesterday.
gaps.hint: a fixed appointment arranged for the future
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am going.

gaps.sentence: They ___ for two hours when the storm hit.
gaps.hint: two hours of walking before the storm
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been walking.

gaps.sentence: He ___ very shy at first, but once you know him he is very chatty.
gaps.hint: seem describes a state not action
gaps.explanation: 'Seem' describes a state and is not used continuously: seems.

gaps.sentence: I ___ her at a conference in 2019, but we did not start working together until last year.
gaps.hint: in 2019 pins a finished past time
gaps.explanation: 'In 2019' is a finished past time, so the past simple is required: met.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ its profits every year since it changed strategy, and analysts expect more growth.
gaps.hint: since clause anchors past to present
gaps.explanation: A 'since' clause connecting a past start to the present requires the present perfect: has increased.
